title: Link an experiment to its data folder
summary: Attach the network folder where an experiment's raw data lives, and open it from the entry in one click.
details: In the Data section of an experiment, paste a network share path (smb://server/share/folder or \\server\share\folder), add an optional label such as "Raw data folder", and press Add.
Each link has buttons to open it on a Mac, to copy the Windows path to paste into Explorer, and to insert a reference to it in the main text.
The label keeps a long path readable. Remove a link with the trash icon while editing.

title: Quick links to LabCollector and your lab's tools
summary: The Links menu in the top bar opens LabCollector and your lab's own pages in one click.
details: Open Links in the top bar to reach LabCollector, OpenIRIS, MoorLab Wiki, ETHIS and MoorLab Zoom. They open in a new tab.
A team admin can change any of these addresses with the pencil icon next to it, so the link always points to the right place.

title: Link templates and see which version you used
summary: Record the template an experiment follows, with or without inserting its content, and keep track of its versions.
details: In an experiment, open Search in the left sidebar and set Type to Experiment templates.
Press Link to associate the template with the experiment without inserting anything, or Add to text to insert its content at the cursor.
Associated templates are listed under Links, each with its version number and how many times it was inserted. Click one to open the template.
Open a template to see its version history and restore an older version; the other versions are kept.

title: Faster scrolling with several spreadsheets
summary: Spreadsheets near the screen now appear as a light preview and become fully editable the moment you click them.
details: Only the table you click gets the full editor, so scrolling past many tables stays smooth.
The preview matches the editor's look, column widths and row heights, so nothing jumps when you click.
The cell you clicked is selected straight away, and the table you are editing stays live while you scroll.
imageAlt: A spreadsheet shown as a light preview with its toolbar; clicking it opens the full editor

highlight.label: Click a table to edit it

title: Tab and Shift+Tab indent several list lines at once
summary: Select multiple bullet or numbered lines and press Tab to indent them all, or Shift+Tab to outdent them.
details: Works for bullet lists, numbered lists and several selected paragraphs.
Nested lists move one level per press.
imageAlt: Several bullet lines selected in the editor; Tab indents them together

title: Version history for templates
summary: See every saved version of a template, compare revisions, and restore an older one without losing the current one.
details: The history opens in a popup on the edit page.
Restoring a version makes it current and keeps the other versions.
Each version has its own edit history that you can restore individually.
imageAlt: The template version history popup listing versions, each with a Restore button and its edit history, outlined

highlight.label: Each version, with Restore and its edit history

title: Insert a spreadsheet of any size, and handier tools in view mode
summary: Drag across a grid to choose the size, like Insert table. View mode now has copy-table and auto-fit buttons.
details: Spreadsheet is also in the classic Insert menu.
Copy the whole table in one click, and auto-fit rows or columns to their content.
Row heights now grow when a narrower column needs more wrapped lines.
imageAlt: The Insert menu with the Spreadsheet size grid and its options, outlined

title: Project management is now Boards, with richer cards
summary: Tasks are now cards, with status badges, deadlines, linked experiments and resources, and bulk actions.
details: Cards show each linked experiment or resource with its status colour.
Select several cards to archive or delete them together.
Steps and comments can be collapsed, and deadlines show how urgent they are.
Duplicate a card into another project, and open a card straight into edit mode.
imageAlt: The Boards page with a card showing its steps and linked experiments, outlined

highlight.label: A card with its steps and linked items

title: Smoother ordering
summary: Attachments can be reused, orders can advance and archive themselves, and notes support lists.
details: Reuse an attachment across orders, and download it with its own button.
Orders can move from requested to ordered when a procurement ID appears, and archive after a set time.
Notes support bulleted and numbered lists, and long titles and file names wrap properly.
imageAlt: The Orders request form with bullet and numbered list buttons above the notes field, outlined

title: More reliable spreadsheet editing
summary: Formulas, fill-drag, undo and cell formatting behave more predictably, in both the inline editor and the popup.
details: Fill-drag keeps absolute references (the ones written with a dollar sign) fixed, so a formula copied down still points at the same cell.
Undo in a spreadsheet only undoes spreadsheet edits, and undo in the text leaves tables alone.
Tab and Enter move between cells, and selected cells and fill-drag are clearly highlighted.
Fixed cell formatting in the popup and a case where saving could blank cells.

Add rows: under a spreadsheet, type how many rows you want and press Add rows to add them at the bottom, up to 50 rows in all. The popup has the same box next to its buttons. Pressing Enter in a cell of the last row also adds a row.
Vertical alignment: select cells and press the top, middle or bottom button next to the left, center, right and justify buttons, in the page and in the popup.
Typing and then adding or deleting a row or column straight away no longer loses what you typed.

Well plates keep their size: rows and columns cannot be added or deleted with Enter, the right-click menu, Add rows or the size boxes, in the page or in the popup. To change the size, pick another plate size in the popup, or choose Custom in its size list to turn the plate into an ordinary spreadsheet.
The cells you select stay selected when you scroll the page.

A plate or spreadsheet shows its row and column labels (1, 2, 3 and A, B, C) before you click it, also for older ones that were saved without them, and rows keep their height when the preview becomes the grid.
A table below the one you add rows to no longer jumps for a moment, and the editor no longer slides a wide plate out of view sideways.
imageAlt: A spreadsheet with a selected cell and its fill handle, outlined, under the spreadsheet toolbar

highlight.label: Selected cell with its fill handle

screenshots.caption: A normal spreadsheet has the Add rows bar under it. A well plate keeps its size, so it has none, and both show their row and column labels

title: A tidier top bar
summary: The navigation bar keeps the key icons visible and folds the rest into a More menu.
details: A Links dropdown groups shortcuts.
The LabCollector link keeps its URL editable from the Tools menu.
imageAlt: The top bar with the More menu open, listing Boards, Orders, Links and Tools

title: Link experiments and resources to your cards
summary: Connect a card to the experiments and resources it is about, and jump between them in one click.
details: Link items while you create a card, or later from the card's detail view.
Use the search panel next to the card to find an experiment or resource, link it, or add it as a step in one move.
Each linked item shows its status colour and type, so you can see at a glance how the work is going.
A project's Linked items section and an All links summary list everything connected to that project, including subprojects.
Click a linked item to open the experiment or resource itself.
imageAlt: A card's detail view with linked experiments and steps, next to the search panel used to link them

title: Better notifications and feedback
summary: You are told when someone gives you access, and the Feedback board can sort by votes or date.
details: Notifications arrive when you gain read access to an experiment or resource, even if you had access before.
The dashboard announcement feed is easier to read.
imageAlt: The notifications dropdown, with a notification that someone gave you access to a resource, outlined

highlight.label: Told when someone shares with you

title: An activity calendar for deadlines and tasks
summary: See every deadline in one calendar: your scheduled tasks together with the unfinished steps of your experiments and resources.
details: Open it from the calendar icon in the left sidebar. A badge counts what is overdue or due within the next hour.
A month grid shows each day's items as small count pills, with clear states for Today, the day you selected, and overdue days. Collapse the grid when you only want the list.
Switch between Day, Week and Month views, and hide weekends if you don't need them. The Today button and 'All visible dates' jump you back or show everything in range.
Below the grid, an agenda lists the items for what you selected, ordered by exact time. Each card says where it came from: a personal task, or a step of an experiment or resource.
Click a step to open its experiment or resource, and mark steps and tasks done right from the agenda, the same way as on the experiment page.
The User and Team switch decides whose experiment and resource steps you see.
Give a task a title, notes, an exact date and time, and a reminder: at the deadline, 15 minutes, 1 hour, 1 day or 1 week before, or a custom number of minutes.
Reminders appear as one grouped, collapsible banner that stays as you move between pages, and they also arrive as notifications and email, following your existing step-deadline preference.
Subscribe to your deadlines from Google Calendar or Apple Calendar with a private link from the Calendar tab. The link is read-only, and you can regenerate or revoke it at any time.
imageAlt: The activity calendar panel in the left sidebar: month grid, Day/Week/Month buttons and legend, outlined

title: A left sidebar with your tools one click away
summary: A slim rail on the left keeps folders, search, to-dos and the calendar open next to your work, on every page.
details: Folders: browse and manage your experiment folders, pin a favorite, and collapse branches you don't need.
Search: your saved filters and results, combined in one place.
Quick search and commands: press Ctrl/Cmd + K from anywhere.
To-do list: tasks and step deadlines sorted by due date, with a count of what is due.
Activity calendar: a Day, Week or Month view of deadlines, with your external calendar.
On experiment pages a table of contents tab lists the headings so you can jump around, and filter sections to print or copy.
The rail stays put while you scroll, and the last panel you opened is remembered.
imageAlt: The left sidebar: the rail of tabs (folders, search, quick search, to-do, calendar) next to an open panel, rail outlined

title: Folders and READMEs
summary: A shared tree of folders for experiments and resources, each with its own README and permissions.
details: fa-folder-tree::Open the Folders tab in the left sidebar. The tree shows every folder; the number next to a folder counts the items inside it.
fa-folder-plus::Press Create folder at the bottom, give it a name (and an optional short description) and choose a parent folder to nest it.

A good way to use them: one folder for each project, and a subfolder inside it for each idea within that project that you want to test and verify. Each approach then has its own place, and you can compare them side by side.
Click a folder to list only what is inside it. Choose the folder when you create an experiment or resource, or change it on its edit page.
fa-ellipsis-vertical::Press the three dots on a folder for Export, Edit (rename, move to another parent, change the description) and Delete. Deleting a folder moves its items to Unfiled.

fa-file-lines::Press the page icon on a folder to open its README: a page of notes for everyone working in that folder. The folder's owner and admins edit it; everyone who can see the folder can read it.
fa-star::Star a folder to bookmark it, and collapse the branches you do not need. The tree remembers what you opened.
fa-arrows-rotate::The Refresh button at the top of the panel loads the folder tree again, for example to see a folder a colleague has just created.
fa-user-shield::Set who can see and edit a folder's contents: open the three dots, press Edit, then Permissions (shown to the folder's owner and admins).

Choose who can see and who can edit with the same options as on a single experiment: a base level, plus teams, user groups or specific people. Leave Include subfolders ticked to cover the whole tree, check the item count the dialog shows, and press Apply.

The permissions of every item you can edit are replaced (items that are not yours, locked or archived are skipped and counted). The folder remembers the choice, so items created in it, moved into it or filed in a new subfolder take the same permissions.
You can still change one experiment on its own afterwards. It stays as you set it until the next Apply on that folder.
imageAlt: The Folders panel with a project folder, its subfolders, and the star, README and menu icons beside each folder
purpose: Keep the lab organised in folders the whole team sees, and decide once who can see and edit everything in a folder.
uses: One folder per project, with a README that lists the project protocols and naming rules.
Inside a project, one subfolder per idea you want to test and verify, so each approach keeps its own experiments and you can compare the results.
Export a whole folder (PDF or ZIP) when a paper is submitted or a person leaves.
Give a project folder read access to the whole team but edit access only to the project members, in one step.
Keep a private folder for drafts that only you and a few colleagues can open.
news: Folders now hold resources as well as experiments, can be bookmarked, have READMEs, can be exported, and can remember permissions that apply to everything inside.
shot: The Folders tab with a project folder open and its README beside it, and the Folder permissions dialog with the Can see tab open

screenshots.caption: The folder README: the owner and admins edit it, and everyone who can see the folder can read it

title: The left sidebar
summary: The row of buttons on the left edge of every page: folders, search, quick search, to-dos, the calendar and the table of contents, one click away.
details: fa-bars::The slim row of buttons on the left edge of every page opens panels next to your page. Click a button to open its panel and click it again to close it. The row stays put while you scroll, and the last panel you opened is remembered. Each panel has its own “i” beside its title with more help.
fa-folder-tree::Folders (the folder tree icon): browse your folders and bookmarks, and manage them.

fa-magnifying-glass::Search (the magnifying glass): search experiments, resources, templates and folders, with your favourite filters. While you edit, its results have buttons to attach an item or paste a link.

fa-bolt::Quick search and commands (the lightning bolt): open it with this button, or press Ctrl + K (Cmd + K on a Mac) on any page, even while typing in the editor. Press Escape or click outside the window to close it.

With the box empty it lists commands. On an edit page these include Save, Save and go back, Insert date, Insert title, Insert note, Insert table or spreadsheet and Insert link. On every page: Open folders, Open filters, Search everything, Open tasks, Open calendar and Open table of contents.

Start typing to narrow the list. It matches the name of a command and the words that describe it, the headings of the entry you are looking at (choosing one scrolls to it), and the folders in your folder tree (choosing one opens it).

After two letters it also searches your experiments and resources by title and lists the matches with their category. Choosing one opens it, and if you have unsaved changes while editing it asks before leaving. Move through the list with the up and down arrow keys and press Enter, or click a result. Up to 24 results are shown.
fa-list-check::To-do list (the checklist icon): your tasks and step deadlines. A red number shows what is overdue or due soon.
fa-calendar-days::Activity calendar (the calendar icon): a Day, Week or Month view of your deadlines and what you finished. A red number shows what is due soon.
fa-bars-staggered::Table of contents (the lines icon): only on an experiment or resource page, it lists the headings so you can jump to one or show only the sections you pick.

fa-bars::On a narrow window the row of buttons would sit on top of your page, so it folds into one button in the top bar, to the left of the eLabFTW logo. Click it to show all the buttons, pick one to open its panel, and the row folds away again. A panel that is open keeps its own button visible so you can close it.
fa-circle-info::The “i” at the bottom of the row opens this guide card.
imageAlt: The left sidebar buttons: folders, quick search, quick actions, to-do, activity calendar and guide
purpose: Keep the tools you use all day next to your work, and get anywhere, or do something, without hunting through menus.
uses: Keep the To-do panel open on a busy day and tick off steps as you finish them.
Keep Folders open while you file new experiments.
Create a new experiment, open the Boards, or jump to an old experiment without leaving the keyboard.
Press Ctrl + K, type a few letters of an old experiment's title and open it.
While writing, press Ctrl + K and choose Insert date, or Save, without reaching for the toolbar.
Jump to a heading in a long experiment by typing part of it.
Open the To-do list or the calendar from the keyboard.
news: One row of buttons with all of these tools on every page, and a keyboard-first quick search and command window.
shot: The left sidebar with the Folders panel open and the row of buttons outlined, and the quick search window open over a page

title: Activity calendar
summary: One calendar for what is coming and what you have already done: your tasks, the steps of your experiments, and the experiments and notes you worked on each day.
details: fa-calendar-days::Open it from the calendar icon in the left sidebar. A badge counts what is overdue or due within the next hour.
A month grid shows each day with small count pills, and marks today, the day you selected and overdue days. Switch between Day, Week and Month views, and hide weekends if you do not need them.
Below the grid, an agenda lists the items for what you selected, in time order. Each card says where it came from: a personal task, or a step of an experiment or resource.

What appears on a day: tasks with a deadline (a finished task stays on its day with the time you finished it); experiment and resource steps with a deadline, and finished steps on the day they were completed (with the time, and a link to the experiment); experiments and resources on their start date; and the headings of an experiment or resource on the day of the date inserted above them (see the next step).

fa-calendar-day::The Day button in the editor toolbar links your notes to this calendar. Each heading you write after an inserted date is listed on that date, under its experiment, until you insert the next date. A heading with no inserted date above it counts under the experiment's start date.
On a day, an experiment lists its headings as a nested outline, so you can see what was done that day. Click a heading to open the experiment at that place.
The User and Team buttons at the top switch between your own items and the whole team's.
The calendar refreshes itself every 30 seconds while the panel is open, so finished steps and new assignments show up by themselves. The Refresh button at the top reloads it right away.

Click a step to open its experiment, and tick steps and tasks off right from the agenda. A completed task stays on its day with the time you finished it, so you can look back at what was done and when.
Add a task with a title, notes, an exact date and time and a reminder (at the deadline, or 15 minutes, 1 hour, 1 day or 1 week before).

Subscribe from Google Calendar or Apple Calendar with the private, read-only link on the Calendar tab. It carries your tasks, your step deadlines and the reminders you set on orders. You can regenerate or revoke it any time.
imageAlt: The Activity calendar panel with a month grid, coloured dots for tasks, experiments and overdue items, and the User and Team switch
purpose: See what is due this week at a glance, never miss a step deadline hidden inside an experiment, and look back at what you finished on earlier days.
uses: Plan the week on Monday: switch to Week view and see every deadline across your experiments.
In a long experiment, press Day before each day's notes. Then look at the month to see which days you worked on it, and what you wrote on each.
Go back to a past week or month to see which tasks you completed and when, for a weekly report or a lab meeting update.
Put the subscription link in your phone calendar so lab deadlines show up next to the rest of your day.
Switch to Team to see what the whole lab is working on this week.
news: New: an activity calendar that combines tasks and experiment steps, with reminders and calendar subscriptions.
shot: The Activity calendar panel with the month grid, the Day/Week/Month buttons and the agenda below

title: Project Boards
summary: Plan lab work as projects of cards, with deadlines and steps, and link each card to its experiments and resources.
details: fa-list-check::Open Boards from the top bar (under More). Create a project, then add cards for the tasks in it.
A card has a title, notes, a deadline, steps, comments and people assigned to it. Status badges and deadline colours show at a glance what needs attention.
Steps and comments can be collapsed to keep a long card short.
Select several cards to archive or delete them together. Duplicate a card into another project, or open a card straight into edit mode.

A project can hold subprojects, for example one for each idea you want to test within it. Drag a project tab onto another to put the projects in the order you want. When a project is finished, archive it from its edit dialog: it leaves the project list but is not deleted, and the archive button next to the project tabs shows archived projects again. To keep a card at the top of its column, open its ⋮ menu and choose Pin to top.
fa-link::To tie a card to the work it is about, open the search panel next to the card while you create it, or later from its detail view.

Find an experiment or resource, then press Link, or add it as a step in one move. Each linked item shows its type icon and a coloured dot for its status, on the card as well as in the project, so you can see how the work is going.
A project's edit dialog has a Linked items section that lists everything connected to that project. Click a linked item to open the experiment or resource itself.

fa-link::All links: the All links button next to Add subproject opens one list of every experiment, resource, template and web address linked to any card in the project, including its subprojects. When a subproject is selected it lists only that subproject, as Links in.

Each row in All links shows the item's type icon and, for experiments and resources, a coloured dot for its status. Click the title to open the item in a new tab. The badge shows which project or subproject it belongs to, and the button on the right shows the card it is linked to: click it to open that card. Press Load more links if the list is long.
imageAlt: A project board with project tabs, the goals, Add subproject and All links buttons, and cards in the To do column
purpose: Keep track of who does what and by when in one board per project, with the plan and the experiments pointing at each other.
uses: One board per paper, grant or project, with a card for each experiment series and each deadline.
A board for lab chores, with a card per task and the person responsible.
Link the protocol template and the experiment for each planned run, and open the project to see which linked experiments are finished.
Press All links on a paper's project to see in one list every experiment and protocol behind it, and open any of them in a click.
news: Boards replace the old project list, with richer cards, bulk actions, subprojects, and cards that link to experiments and resources with their status colours.
shot: The Boards page with a project open and one card showing its steps and linked experiments, and the search panel used to link them

title: Orders
summary: Track things to order for the team, from request to delivery.
details: fa-cart-shopping::Open Orders from the top bar (under More) and press New order. Say what you need, with the supplier and any link or catalogue number.
fa-paperclip::Add the supplier details and notes (lists are supported), and attach quotes or invoices. An attachment can be reused on other orders.

fa-clone::Copy an order: press the copy button on an order to fill the request form at the top with its title, notes, linked resources and tags. Change what you need and press Request order. The files are not copied; add them as described next.

fa-share::Attach a previous attachment: on an order that already has a file, press the arrow button beside the file (Add to new order). It joins the attachments of the order you are writing, and a copy is attached when you press Request order, so you do not have to download and upload it again.

Statuses: an order is Requested (asked for), Ordered (placed with the supplier), Received (it has arrived), Backlogged (known to be needed but not requested yet) or Cancelled. Change it with the coloured dropdown at the top of the order.
Tabs: All, Requested, Ordered, Received, Backlogged and Cancelled show one status at a time. All shows everything that is not archived. Archived holds the orders you have archived.
To change several orders at once, tick them and use Move to status… in the bar that appears.
Ordered and Received orders show a Missing Procurement ID warning when no procurement ID was found in an attached file.
The person who placed an order is notified when someone else changes its status.
fa-thumbtack::Pin an order by hand to keep it at the top of the list, on every tab, until you unpin it.

fa-bookmark::Pinned for all and Reference are two special kinds of order with no status and no dropdown. Pinned for all is shared with the team and stays at the top for everyone. Reference is only for you: nobody else sees it, and it stays at the top of the All tab for you. Each has its own tab and does not show on the status tabs.

Tick Pinned for all or Reference when you create an order, or later when you edit it. Once an order is one of them it cannot go back to Requested, Ordered or another status. You can switch it between the two in the edit form (the author or a team admin; only the author can make an order a Reference).
You can set a reminder on an order.

fa-envelope-open-text::Templates: the Templates tab on the Orders page holds texts that go with ordering, such as an email to a supplier or a quote request. Everyone in the team can search them and copy the text; the author or a team admin edits them.
imageAlt: Orders in three statuses (Requested, Ordered, Received) with their colored status dropdowns and the copy, edit and archive buttons
purpose: One place to request what the lab needs and to see where each order is, instead of emails and sticky notes.
uses: Request a reagent, attach the supplier quote and other links, information and files related to the order.
Mark an order Received when it arrives, so the list always shows what is still on its way.
Keep a supplier's catalogue number or standing order details as a Reference of your own, or as Pinned for all for the whole team.
Keep a standard quote-request email as a template, copy it, fill in the supplier and the product, and send it from your mail program.
Copy last month's order for the same supplier, adjust the quantity, and attach the previous quote with the arrow button instead of searching for the file.
news: New: reusable attachments, reminders, notes with lists, the Pinned for all and Reference kinds, and shared text templates for supplier emails.
shot: The Orders page with a few orders at different stages and one order open

title: Link items to experiments
summary: Connect an experiment to the resources, data folders and templates it uses.
details: Scroll below the main text. Each section opens and closes on its own.
fa-list-check::Steps and tasks: a checklist for the experiment, with deadlines that also show in your calendar.

fa-at::Mention people in a step: type @ in the add-a-step box or in a step's text, then pick a name with the arrow keys and Tab (or the mouse). Each person you mention gets the step as a to-do of their own, linked to the experiment and with the step's deadline, and a notification that you assigned it.

fa-circle-check::When a step is done: if one of the people you mentioned ticks their to-do, the step is completed on the experiment and on everyone else's to-do as well, and you and the other assignees are told. Ticking the step on the experiment does the same. Taking a name out of the step removes that person's to-do, and deleting the step removes them all.

Data: link the network folder where the experiment’s raw data lives. Paste the path (smb://server/share/folder or \\server\share\folder), add an optional label such as “Raw data folder” and press Add.
Each data link has buttons to open it on a Mac, to copy the Windows path to paste into Explorer, and to insert a reference to it in the main text. Remove a link with the trash icon while editing.
fa-link::Links: other experiments, associated templates, resources, orders, web addresses and LabCollector entries this one relates to.
fa-paperclip::Files / folders and Local files: attach files, or paste references to files kept elsewhere.
Compounds and Custom fields: record chemicals from the compound database, and any extra fields your team defined.
On an experiment, the LabCollector links section lists the LabCollector entries it relates to.
imageAlt: An experiment page with the Steps and tasks section and the Links section showing a linked experiment and a linked resource
purpose: Record not only what you did but also what you used, where the data lives and what it relates to.
uses: Link the resources you refer to, such as the record of the meeting where the experiment was planned, so anyone can follow the trail.
Add a step with a deadline for the next measurement and see it in the calendar.
Link the folder with the microscope images or the sequencing run, and insert the reference where you describe the measurement.
news: New: the Data section for network folders, and order, template and LabCollector links in these sections.
shot: An experiment page scrolled to the sections under the main text with the Data section open

title: Steps and tasks
summary: Break an experiment into steps, give a step to colleagues with @, and see when it is done.
details: fa-list-check::Steps and tasks sit under the main text of an experiment, template or resource. Type a step in the box at the bottom and press Enter or Add a step. Tick it when it is done: the time is kept. Drag a step by its handle to reorder it, click its text to edit it, and use the trash icon to remove it.
fa-clock::Open a step with the arrow on its right to set a deadline and a reminder. A step with a deadline shows in the to-do list and on that day in the Activity calendar.

fa-at::Give a step to someone: type @ in the step and pick a name. Move through the names with the arrow keys and press Tab (or click one). Mention several people and each of them gets the step. You become the assigner.

fa-list-check::What each person gets: a to-do of their own, called “Step: …”, linked to the experiment and carrying the step's deadline, and a notification that you assigned it. They can open the experiment from their to-do. Someone who cannot open the entry still gets the to-do and sees the entry's name.

fa-pen::Change the step later and their to-dos follow: edit the text and it updates; add a name and that person gets the step; take a name out and their to-do is removed; set, change or remove the deadline and it is copied or cleared on their to-dos. Deleting the step removes all of them.

fa-circle-check::Finishing: when any one of the people you mentioned ticks their to-do, or anyone with edit rights ticks the step on the experiment, the step is completed for everybody: the step is ticked and every assignee's to-do is done. Unticking reopens all of it.

fa-bell::Who is told when a step is completed: you (the assigner) and the other people it was given to, not the person who did it, and nobody else on the experiment. Choose web or email for these in Settings > Notifications (assigned a step, and a step was completed). Web is on by default and email is off.
fa-calendar-days::In the Activity calendar a step with a deadline appears on that day, and a finished step appears on the day it was completed, with a link to the experiment.
fa-user-lock::Who can do what: you need edit rights on the entry to add, edit, tick or delete its steps. The people you give a step to can tick their own to-do without edit rights on the entry.
fa-comment::The same @ list works in the comments of an experiment, template or resource: the person you mention is notified if they can read the entry.
imageAlt: A step "Load the gel @Bob Tester @Srivathsan Adivarahan" in the Steps and tasks section of an experiment
purpose: Hand a part of an experiment to a colleague and see when it is done, without chasing them.
uses: Ask a colleague to prepare the buffers and be told when they are ready.
Give a step to two people and have it close for both as soon as one of them finishes.
Put a deadline on a step so it shows in everyone's calendar.
news: New: assign a step with @, the person gets it as a to-do, and finishing it tells you.
shot: An experiment's Steps and tasks section with a step that mentions two people, next to one of their to-do lists showing it

title: Templates and their versions
summary: Link a template to an experiment, see which version you used, and restore older versions.
details: In an experiment, open Search in the left sidebar and set Type to Experiment templates.
fa-link::Press Link to record the template without inserting anything, or Add to text to insert its content at the cursor.
Associated templates are listed under Links with their version number and how many times they were inserted. Click one to open it.

fa-code-branch::Publish new version: when a template is in a state you want to keep, press Publish new version in its toolbar. Published versions are numbered (Version 1, 2, 3...) and never overwritten.
fa-clock-rotate-left::Version history: open a template and press Version history to list every published version with who published it and when. Click the plus beside a version to read its content.

Name and notes: give each version a short name (for example “Added analysis steps”) and notes on what changed, with the Edit button next to it. They are saved with the template and included in backups and exports.
fa-rotate-left::Restore a version: press Restore next to a version to make the template look like it did then. Nothing is lost, the other versions are kept.

fa-list::Edit history: every version also has an Edit history list of the smaller changes saved while it was being worked on. Each one can be read and restored on its own, so you can go back to a single edit within a version, not just to the version itself.
fa-code-compare::Compare: tick two entries, in the versions or inside an Edit history, and press Compare revisions to see what changed between them.
fa-star::Star the templates you use most to find them quickly.
imageAlt: The version history of a template: a named version with notes and its Edit history, each with a Restore button
purpose: Start from the lab’s standard protocol and know exactly which version of it an experiment followed.
uses: Keep the standard protocol as a template and publish a new version when it changes.
Months later, see which experiments used the old version.
news: New: template versions with names and notes, version history, restoring a version or a single edit, and template links on experiments.
shot: The template version history with the list of versions and the Restore buttons

title: Feedback board
summary: Post ideas and bugs, upvote the ones that matter, and discuss them with your team.
details: fa-lightbulb::Open Feedback from the top bar and post an idea or a problem for your team, with a title and a description.
fa-star::Choose Feature for an idea, or Bug for a problem. The two buttons above the list also filter it.
fa-caret-up::Upvote the items that matter most to you. You automatically upvote your own post.
fa-arrow-up::Sort the list by Most votes or by date.
fa-comment::Open an item to read and write comments. Type @ followed by a name to mention a colleague, who is then notified.
fa-pen::The author of an item, or a team admin, can edit it, change its status (open, planned, done or declined) and delete it.
fa-bell::You are notified when someone mentions you in feedback.
imageAlt: The Feedback board with the form to post a feature or bug, the filter tabs and one post with its vote button and comments
purpose: Tell the people who run the system what would help, and see what the team cares about most.
uses: Ask for a new field or a new link, and see how many colleagues want it too.
Report something that does not work, and follow it as it goes from open to planned to done.
news: New: a feedback board with votes, statuses and comments.
shot: The Feedback board sorted by votes, with one item open and its comments

title: Search, favourite filters and linking
summary: Search with your favourite filters, then attach what you find to an experiment or paste a link to it, without leaving the page.
details: fa-magnifying-glass::Open the Search tab in the left sidebar. Pick a Type (All, Experiments, Resources, Experiment templates or Resource templates) and type in the search box.
The Filters list shows your favourite categories, tags, statuses and owners for that type. Tick the ones you want and press Apply filters.
Press Manage to choose which ones are your favourites. They are saved only for your account.
Results appear below, with a link to the full list.

fa-link::Attach while editing: open an experiment or resource in edit mode, search in the panel, and press the link button on a result to attach that experiment or resource to the one you are editing. It then shows under Links.
Paste a link: press the second button on a result to put a link to it into the text, at the cursor.
For templates, the link button records the template an experiment came from, and the second button inserts the template's content at the cursor instead of a link.
With a board card open, results also get a button to link them to that card, and one to add them as a step on it.
imageAlt: The Search panel open beside an experiment being edited, listing results with a link button and a paste-a-link button on each
purpose: Stop re-entering the same filters every time you look for something, and link what you find into your work in one click.
uses: Favourite your own tags and the statuses you use, then filter “my running experiments” in two clicks.
Switch Type to Resources to look through meeting records and other resources with the same panel.
While writing up an experiment, search for its protocol template and press the link button to record it, then paste a link to the earlier experiment next to the sentence that refers to it.
Search a template while editing and insert its content straight into the experiment.
news: New: filters you can favourite, shared by search across experiments, resources and templates, plus attach and paste-a-link buttons on every result.
shot: The Search panel next to an experiment being edited, with the attach and paste-a-link buttons on a result outlined

title: Table of contents in experiments
summary: A list of the headings of an experiment so you can jump around, show only the sections you pick, and print or copy only parts of it.
details: fa-bars-staggered::On an experiment page, open the Table of Contents tab in the left sidebar.
The Document sections list shows the headings. Click one to jump to it.
Use Add filter or Add heading filter to select sections, and choose whether all or any of the filters must match.
To read only some parts, open Select headings to filter or print and tick the headings you want. The experiment then shows just those sections and hides the rest, until you clear the selection.
fa-print::Press Print selection or Copy filtered content to get only those parts. Switch spreadsheets and pictures on or off.
imageAlt: An experiment with the Table of Contents panel open and three headings ticked, showing only those parts of the text
purpose: Long experiments become easy to move through, and you can share just the part someone needs.
uses: Copy just the Methods part of an experiment into an email.
Print the results sections of a long experiment for a meeting.
Tick only the Results headings to read them without scrolling past the methods.
news: New: a contents tab with section filters, print and copy.
shot: An experiment with the Table of Contents panel open and a few headings selected

highlight.label: Tick headings to filter, print or copy

title: Notifications
summary: A bell that tells you what needs you, so you do not have to check every page.
details: fa-bell::The bell in the top bar collects your notifications and shows how many are new.
fa-user-check::You are notified when someone gives you access to an experiment or resource, mentions you in a comment, assigns you a task or a card, or changes the status of an order.
fa-gear::Choose how you receive each kind of notification: open your Settings from the user menu in the top bar and go to the Notifications tab. Every kind of notification has two switches.
fa-bell::Web: the notification appears in the bell inside eLabFTW.
fa-envelope::Email: the same notification is also sent to your email address. Switch Email off for a kind to receive it only in the app, or switch Web off to receive it only by email.
fa-toggle-on::The All notifications row at the top switches every kind on or off at once for Web, or for Email.
fa-envelope::Step deadlines can also arrive by email, following your existing preference.
imageAlt: The notifications dropdown from the bell, with Clear all, Notification history and Notification settings
purpose: Be told when something changes for you, without checking every page.
uses: Share an experiment and the person you shared it with gets a notification right away.
Mention a colleague with @name in a card comment and they are notified.
Keep Web on for everything, and Email on only for the few that need your attention even when you are not in eLabFTW, such as a deadline or an order status change.
news: New: notifications for assignments, mentions and access.
shot: The notifications dropdown open from the bell in the top bar

title: The editor toolbar
summary: New buttons above the text of an experiment: one Insert menu, dates, titles, notes, checklists, spreadsheets and more.
details: fa-floppy-disk::Save: the first button saves the experiment, and the bar shows whether your changes are saved. Save and go back is in the File menu.

fa-plus::Insert: one menu for everything you can add. It lists Insert note, Divider, Tables, Spreadsheet, Well plate, Image, Links and Insert template. Title and date have their own buttons next to it. Insert template is only here, not as a separate button.
fa-list-check::Checklist: turns lines into tick boxes. Type [ ] and a space to start one, then click a box to tick it.

fa-image::Image: in the Insert menu. Opens the picture window to add an image from your computer or a web address, with a description and size. Image options: this button is only on the toolbar while an image is selected. It opens the same window for that image, to change its description, size or caption.
fa-link::Links: in the Insert menu, under Links. Add a web link, upload and link a file or folder, refer to a file or folder on a shared drive, or link a LabCollector item.

fa-calendar-day::Day: inserts today's date in your saved format, and links your notes to the Activity calendar: the headings you write after an inserted date appear on that day in the calendar, until you insert the next date. The arrow gives Custom date, Log entry (date and time), and Edit, Copy link and Delete for a date you selected. Double-click a date to edit it.

fa-heading::Insert title (the heading button): opens a window where you set the title text and style (font, size, colour, alignment, how it appears in the table of contents) and press Insert title. Press Save style to keep the style under a name; with a title or text selected, open the arrow beside the button and choose a saved style to apply it to the selection. Ctrl+Alt+T opens the same window.
fa-minus::Divider: in the Insert menu. Single or double, solid or dashed lines to separate parts of your notes.
fa-note-sticky::Note: in the Insert menu. Inserts a highlighted note box with your saved note settings.

fa-pen-to-square::Note options: this button is only on the toolbar while your cursor is inside a note. It opens a window for that note: its title, whether the title appears in the Table of Contents, and the heading level. Apply changes that note only; the text inside it stays as it is.

fa-table::Spreadsheet tools: this button is only on the toolbar while a spreadsheet is selected. It edits and formats that spreadsheet: edit it, open it in the Spreadsheet Editor, autofit column widths and row heights, change the table and cell style, indent or outdent it and make it sortable. To put in a new table, spreadsheet or well plate, use Insert.

fa-copy::Copy table: in the Edit menu of the menu bar, next to Copy and Paste. Copy complete table copies a whole table with its formatting, ready to paste into another program; Copy selected text and tables copies your selection.
fa-file-lines::Insert template: in the Insert menu. Opens a window to insert a template into the experiment, at your cursor. See the steps below.

fa-magnifying-glass::In the template window, type in the search box to narrow the list, and switch between Mine, Favourites and All. Press the star beside a template to add or remove it from your favourites.
fa-hand-pointer::Click a template's title to insert it straight away. Its content goes into the text exactly as it is in the template, with a line break after it.

fa-list-ol::To insert several at once, tick their boxes, set how many times each should be inserted (1 to 20), and press Insert selected. They go in top to bottom in the order of the list, each repeated as many times as you chose.

fa-clock-rotate-left::Version: every template has a version picker. Leave it on Latest, or choose an older published version, shown with its number, date and who published it, to insert exactly the version you want to follow.

fa-link::Link in the template window records the template as used by this experiment, without inserting its text. It shows under Associated experimental templates. Inserting a template records it too, so the template's own list of where it is used includes this experiment.

toolbar-format-painter::Format painter: right after the text colour and highlight buttons, before the alignment buttons. Copy the look of some text, then select other text and press it again to apply it.
toolbar-clear-formatting::Clear formatting: next to the format painter. Strips the formatting from the selected text.
fa-keyboard::Keyboard shortcuts: Ctrl+Shift+D date and time, Ctrl+Alt+T title window, Ctrl+Alt+N note, Ctrl+Shift+H single line, Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H double line.
fa-thumbtack::On a long experiment the toolbar stays at the top as you scroll and slides smoothly with the top bar.
fa-circle-info::The “i” at the very end of the toolbar opens this guide card.
imageAlt: The editor toolbar with the Insert menu open, listing Insert note, Divider, Tables, Spreadsheet, Well plate, Image, Links and Insert template
purpose: Find every editing tool in one place, and write and structure an experiment faster with fewer clicks.
uses: Open the arrow beside Day and choose Log entry each time you return to an experiment so that your notes read as a dated record.
Press Day before each new day's notes, so that every heading under it lands on the right day in the Activity calendar.
Start a protocol step list with a checklist, then tick the boxes off at the bench.
Insert a note box with a clear title for a warning or a deviation so that it shows up in the table of contents.
Press Insert, then Insert template, search for your protocol, and click its title to start the experiment from it.
Tick a protocol and a results table together, press Insert selected, and get your usual starting set in one go.
Set the quantity to 3 on a template to insert it three times, once for each replicate.
Choose an older version of a protocol to repeat an experiment exactly as it was done before.
Mark the templates you use all the time with a star, then use the Favourites tab.
Save a title style (for example a bold blue heading for each day), then select a heading and apply it from the arrow beside the heading button.
news: New: one Insert menu (note, divider, tables, spreadsheets, well plates, links and templates), a Note options button that appears while a note is selected, Spreadsheet tools that appear while a spreadsheet is selected, checklists, and a format painter next to the colours.
shot: The editor toolbar with the Insert menu open

highlight.label: Spreadsheet, Well plate, Image, Links and Insert template

screenshots.caption: Note options appears on the toolbar while your cursor is inside a note
Note options: change the note's title, whether it is in the Table of Contents, and the heading level
Spreadsheet tools appears while a spreadsheet is selected: edit and format it from here. A well plate below has its size fixed, so it has no Add rows bar

title: Working together: members, assignments and comments
summary: Add colleagues to a project, assign cards to people, and talk about the work in comments where you can @mention anyone.
details: fa-user-group::Open a project's edit dialog and use Team members on this project to add colleagues. Remove someone with the × on their name.
A subproject starts with the same members as its parent. Members of a parent project can already see and manage its subprojects, and you can still add more people to a subproject.
fa-user::Open a card and choose people under Assigned to. You can assign several people, and remove one with the ×. Left empty, the card is assigned to you.
Each assigned person gets a notification, and the card shows who created it and who it was assigned by. Use Assigned to me above the board to see just your cards.
Cards assigned to you also appear in the To-do tab in the left sidebar.
fa-comment::Comments: every card has a Comments section. Write a comment, and type @ followed by a name to mention someone. The person you mention is notified.
The same comments with @mentions work on tasks in the To-do list and on posts in the Feedback board. You can edit or delete your own comments.
Cards show a comment count, so you can see which ones have a discussion going without opening them.
imageAlt: A board card with two assigned people and a comment that mentions a colleague with @
purpose: See who is working on a project and who looks after each card, and keep the conversation right next to the work it is about.
uses: Add the whole project team once, then assign a card to the person who will run each experiment.
Ask a question on a card with @name, so the person gets a notification and the answer stays with the card.
Create a subproject for one paper figure and let it start with the same people as the main project.
news: New: project members, several people per card, comments with @mentions, and notifications when you are assigned or mentioned.
shot: A card open with the Assigned to field and the Comments section showing an @mention

title: To-do list
summary: Your tasks and the deadlines of your experiment steps in one list: add, remind, tick off, look back, and subscribe from your own calendar.
details: fa-list-check::Open the To-do list from the checklist button in the left sidebar. The red number on the button counts what is overdue or due soon. The refresh button reloads the list.
The panel has two tabs. Tasks is the list; Calendar shows a month and the tasks of the day you pick.
The Tasks list is grouped by due date: Overdue, Today, Tomorrow, then each later day, and No due date at the end. It mixes your own tasks with the steps of your experiments that have a deadline.

The list refreshes itself every 30 seconds while the page is open, so what others did (a finished step, a new assignment) appears without pressing refresh. It waits while you are typing in a field of the panel.
A step shows the name of its experiment, and an Add a deadline link when it has no deadline yet. Click the step to open the experiment. Ticking it marks the step complete in the experiment.

fa-plus::Add a task: type it in the box at the top and press Enter or the plus button. Press the arrow beside the box for more: notes, the board project it belongs to, a date and a time, and a reminder. Next to the date, the Today button sets today's date, and a time if none is set yet.
Reminders: at the deadline, or 15 minutes, 1 hour, 1 day or 1 week before, or after a number of minutes you choose, or at a specific date and time. A reminder needs a date and time first.

fa-repeat::Repeat: set a task to repeat, as in Google Tasks. Choose Daily, Weekly, Every weekday (Monday to Friday), Monthly, Yearly or Custom: every number of days, weeks, months or years, and for weeks the days you want, such as Monday, Wednesday and Friday. Choose when it ends: never, on a date, or after a number of times. A repeating task needs a date and a time, and you can set it when you add a task and when you edit one.

When you complete a repeating task, the next one is created with the same text, people, project and links, and the date moved on from the previous date, not from the day you ticked it. A task that was late gets its next date in the future, so late ones do not pile up. Repeating tasks show a repeat icon, and the details say how often. Tasks that a step created with an @mention cannot repeat.
fa-grip-vertical::Each row has a handle to drag it into a new order or onto another day, a button to edit it, and Done to tick it off. Click the task's title to open its details.
In a task's details you can add a description and notes (bold, italic, headings, bullet and numbered lists, links), link items, add steps and write comments.

Linked items: press Open Search to link and use the link buttons on the results to attach experiments, resources and templates. You can also add a web address or a network folder (smb://) with a label. On a Mac the network folder opens directly; on Windows you can copy its path to paste into Explorer.
Steps: break a task into smaller steps and tick them off one by one. Comments: write a note to your colleagues and type @ followed by a name to mention someone, who is then notified.
At the bottom of the details: Archive (puts the task away), Duplicate (a copy to adjust), Delete (asks first and cannot be undone), and Edit.
Done tasks move to Completed tasks below the list. Choose how far back to look, from the past day to the past month, and press Restore to bring one back.
Archived tasks, also below the list, holds the tasks you archived. Open it to see them and press Unarchive to bring one back.
fa-calendar::The Calendar tab shows a month. Pick a day to see its tasks and the tasks you completed on it, and move between months with the arrows.

Subscribe from your own calendar: on the Calendar tab press Create private link, then add it to Google Calendar or Apple Calendar. The link is read-only and shows your task titles and deadlines, so keep it private. You can regenerate or revoke it at any time. Google Calendar needs the link to be reachable from the internet.
Board cards assigned to you appear in this list as well. The Project boards button above the list opens the boards. When someone assigns you a task, you get a notification from the bell.
imageAlt: The to-do panel adding a task with a custom weekly repeat on Monday and Thursday, with the Today button next to the date
purpose: Know what is due today and never lose a step deadline inside an experiment.
uses: Start the day by opening the list and ticking off what is done.
Add a task with a reminder the moment you think of it, such as ordering a reagent by Friday.
Keep the list open on a busy day and tick off steps as you finish them.
Link the experiment and the network folder with the raw data to a task, so everything for it is one click away.
On Friday, open Completed tasks for the past week to see what you finished, for a report or a meeting.
Put the private calendar link in your phone's calendar so your deadlines appear next to the rest of your day.
Make a chore that comes back, such as ordering buffer every Monday, repeat, and tick it off each time.
news: New: one list for tasks and step deadlines with reminders, steps and comments on tasks, linked items, a completed and archived history, a calendar view, and a calendar subscription.
shot: Adding a task with Repeat set to every week on Monday and Thursday

title: Announcements
summary: Lab news at the top of your dashboard: read it, react to it, and look back at earlier announcements.
details: fa-bullhorn::The Announcements feed is on the right of the dashboard. A new announcement carries a New badge until you have seen it, and a bell notification tells you when one is posted.
fa-circle-info::A blue circle marks an announcement for information.
fa-triangle-exclamation::A warning triangle marks something that needs attention.
fa-thumbtack::A pin means it was pinned to stay at the top of the feed.

fa-up-right-from-square::Click the title to open the announcement on its own page. Long texts are shortened: press Show more to read all of it. Pictures and attached files appear with the announcement.
fa-face-smile::React with the small face button under an announcement, which opens a choice of reactions. You can pick several. Reactions that others picked show as small counters you can click too.
fa-clock-rotate-left::See previous announcements, under the feed, lists the older ones.
fa-plus::Team admins write announcements with the plus button above the feed. In the feed they can also edit an announcement (the pen) and pin or unpin it (the pin).
imageAlt: The Announcements feed on the dashboard with pinned announcements, their reactions and the plus button to write one
purpose: Make sure everyone hears about lab news, maintenance and changes, without relying on emails that get lost.
uses: Read the latest lab news every time you open the dashboard.
Pin the lab meeting schedule so that it always stays at the top.
React with a thumbs-up to confirm you have read a change.
news: New: an announcement feed on the dashboard with reactions, pinning, pictures and files.
shot: The dashboard with the Announcements feed on the right, showing a pinned announcement and its reactions

title: Experiments
summary: Where your experiments live: create them, find them, and see everything you can do with one.
details: fa-flask::Open Experiments from the top bar, or from the Experiments heading on the dashboard. The list shows your team's experiments with the most recent first.
fa-plus::Create an experiment with the Create button at the top right of the list, or the plus in the top bar. Choose the type, give it a title and pick its folder.

fa-magnifying-glass::Find experiments with the search bar above the list or with the Search panel in the left sidebar. Filter by category, status, owner, visibility, date, tags and custom fields, and sort by newest, least recently modified, ID, custom ID or rating.

fa-square-check::Tick several experiments to act on them together: archive, delete or lock them, change their category, status or permissions, export them (for example as CSV, JSON or an ELN archive), or link them to a resource or another experiment.

fa-pencil::Open an experiment to read it. Edit opens the edit page, where you write the main text and fill the sections below it (see the Link items to experiments, Editor toolbar and Table of contents cards).
fa-floppy-disk::On the edit page, Save keeps your changes and shows when they were last saved; Save and go back also returns to the experiment.
fa-clone::Duplicate makes a copy of an experiment to start a new one from.
fa-signature::Add signature signs the content of the experiment with your key.
fa-lock::Lock freezes an experiment so that nobody changes it by accident; unlock it to edit again.
fa-calendar-check::Timestamp stores proof that the experiment existed at that moment. Every timestamp is kept as an attachment.
fa-ellipsis-vertical::The three dots hold the less common actions: See changelog, Transfer ownership, Create template from entry, Archive, Delete and, for a deleted experiment, Restore.
fa-people-arrows::Transfer ownership gives an experiment to a colleague. Create template from entry turns a finished experiment into a template.
fa-box-archive::Archive puts a finished experiment away without deleting it; Unarchive brings it back.
imageAlt: The Experiments list with two experiments ticked and the bulk-action bar open above them
purpose: Keep every experiment in one searchable place, from the first idea to the finished record.
uses: Start a new experiment from a similar one with Duplicate.
Filter by status and owner to see which of your experiments are still running.
Tick all the experiments of a finished project and export them together.
Lock an experiment once the results are final.
news: Experiments can be organised in folders, linked to orders and resources, and read in a table of contents.
shot: The Experiments list with the search bar, a few experiments ticked, and the bulk-action bar open

title: Resources
summary: Where your team keeps records that are not experiments, such as meetings, and how to find and use them.
details: fa-cubes-stacked::Open Resources from the top bar, or from the Resources heading on the dashboard. A resource is a record that is not an experiment, for example the record of a meeting.
fa-plus::Create a resource with the Create button at the top right of the list, or the plus in the top bar. Choose the type, give it a title and pick its folder.
fa-magnifying-glass::Find resources with the search bar above the list or with the Search panel in the left sidebar, with the same filters and sorting as for experiments.

fa-square-check::Tick several resources to archive, delete or lock them, change their category, status or permissions, export them, or link them to an experiment or another resource. A resource can also be made bookable or not from here.
fa-pencil::Open a resource to read it. Edit opens the edit page, with the same main text, editor toolbar and sections as an experiment.
fa-clone::Duplicate makes a copy of a resource, for example to prepare the next meeting from the last one.
fa-lock::Lock freezes a resource so that nobody changes it by accident.
fa-calendar-plus::Book item opens the scheduler to reserve a resource that can be booked. Modify booking parameters sets how it can be booked.
fa-cart-shopping::A resource can be set up to be ordered: Create procurement request starts an order for it.
fa-link::In an experiment's Links section, link the resources it relates to, so anyone can follow the trail.
fa-ellipsis-vertical::The three dots hold the less common actions: See changelog, Transfer ownership, Create template from entry, Archive, Delete and, for a deleted resource, Restore.
imageAlt: A resource opened for reading, with its toolbar: edit, duplicate, book, sign, timestamp, order and download
purpose: Keep the shared records of the lab, such as meetings, in one place that anyone can search and link to.
uses: Keep one resource per group meeting, with the agenda and the decisions, and link it from the experiments that came out of it.
Duplicate last meeting's resource to prepare the next one.
Search the Resources type in the Search panel to find an earlier meeting by a word from its title.
news: Resources can be organised in folders, linked to experiments and orders, and found from the left sidebar.
shot: The Resources list with a few resources, and one open with its toolbar
